subject: Provisioning patterns, IP escrow, and service-account handoff — kickoff
messages:
From: Tom Hsu <tom@vaultline.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@vaultline.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Vaultline onboarding — provisioning patterns, IP escrow, and SA handoff

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo. We're ready to move into the full onboarding sprint but have a couple of access/ops asks we want to resolve up front so the CS <> Engineering handoff is clean. High level:

- We need a recommended service-account pattern for our CI/CD pipelines (short-lived vs. long-lived).
- Our security team requests an "IP escrow" plan: a way to maintain an allowlist for staging and prod that we can programmatically update during scheduled windows.
- SCIM mapping: our HR system exports usernames without domain suffixes; we need a field map that avoids collisions across multiple orgs under our account.

Attached is a template that shows our current provisioning CSV and our current IP ranges. Can your onboarding/ops team propose a minimal runbook and a timeline for handoff to Eng? We hope to cut over in the week of May 10.

Tom
Operations Lead | Vaultline

Attachments: vaultline-mapping-template.xlsx (spreadsheet), ip-allowlist-format.txt (text)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hsu <tom@vaultline.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 18:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vaultline onboarding — provisioning patterns, IP escrow, and SA handoff

Tom — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we need. We're aligned to put together a short runbook and a small demo of the provisioning pattern for your SREs. Quick answers up front:

1) Service accounts: we typically recommend short-lived workload identities (rotated via your KMS) for CI jobs that perform write actions, plus a small set of long-lived machine identities for observability/monitoring where human rotation is disruptive. We'll propose a mapping by role and action.

2) IP escrow: we can support a scheduled ACL update flow using our deploy pipeline, or we can set up a managed allowlist hosted in a customer-facing bucket + webhook that your ops team controls. Both approaches have trade-offs (latency vs. auditability).

3) SCIM: we'll create a suggested SCIM attribute map that uses vaultline:org_id + uid to avoid collisions. We'll include fallback logic for missing domain suffixes.

I'll put together a 1-page runbook and schedule a 45-minute walkthrough with Eng + Ops next Tue (May 11) at 10am PT. Marissa / Ben — can you confirm availability and whether we should include any legal or security folks?

Thanks,
Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Vaultline onboarding — provisioning patterns, IP escrow, and SA handoff

On Thu, Apr 22, 2027 at 6:04 PM Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Tom — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we need. We're aligned to put together a short runbook and a small demo of the provisioning pattern for your SREs.

All good from CS — I'll handle collecting the security attendees. Ben, can you prepare the sample service-account role matrix and a short script to demonstrate an "IP escrow update" (atomic allowlist swap) during the demo? Keep it to <10 lines so we can show it live.

Also adding a note: we should surface the audit log retention expectations and the KMS key policy for Vaultline's legal team. I'll draft the invite and include Legal:security@vaultline.com unless you want a named contact.

Marissa
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom@vaultline.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Vaultline onboarding — provisioning patterns, IP escrow, and SA handoff

Marissa / Soojin / Tom — thanks, I'll prep the artifacts. Quick plan from Eng:

- Deliverables before demo (May 11): role-to-permission matrix (CSV), a short-lived SA rotation demo (two-step example with KMS), and a CI job example using workload identity.
- IP escrow demo: show a commit-driven allowlist (Git -> webhook -> atomic swap) and an alt: serverless webhook that takes authorized requests to add/remove ranges.
- SCIM mapping: propose using custom attribute "vaultline_org" + externalId; we'll include a reconciliation job example for duplicates.

Tom — can you confirm whether Vaultline CI runs on GitHub Actions or an internal runner? That will determine the exact impl for workload identity.

I'll attach the sample scripts to the invite.

Ben Carter
Platform Engineering | Redwood Inference
